updated_note: Edited by hand at the end of each stage; the page builder reads it.

stages.name: One split with a trained encoder
stages.question: Does the paper's single split work in our own code?
stages.result: Yes. Passes on all 5 seeds. The authors' own script also run: our numbers are close to theirs (about 0.01 lower on R²).

stages.name: Split a second time
stages.question: B1: does the second split work given correct pairs? B2: can those pairs be built from the data?
stages.result: B1: second split works with correct pairs (15 seeds). B2 (spec run, 18 runs): pairs built from clusters cost little (angle +1.3 deg vs B1) when clusters are right, but the world is too hard for the gates (B1 misses them too) and the split breaks below purity ~0.8. Update 2026-10-21: cluster count fixed in the slow subspace (E31/E32, boundary sigma_cat 0.4); rung gate for failed rungs (E33 confirmed); generic MLP encoder splits when it keeps every block (E25-E30), but a stronger regulariser does not make it keep them (E35).

stages.name: Deeper ladder and scaling
stages.question: How many levels hold up, and does error shrink with more data?
stages.result: Depth 4 and 5 recover every block (angles 0.6-2.1 deg, gap ratios 47-73; E34); the strict leakage test is the first check to fail with depth; angle is flat at about 1.25 deg from 10^4 to 10^6 pairs (no 1/sqrt(n) fall). Robot data (E24, E36): the viewpoint factor does not form a clean block with frozen features, even at the paper's block sizes; fine-tuning needs a GPU.

stages.name: Does it help?
stages.question: Does the ladder beat other methods at the same cost?
stages.result: Not attempted as planned. Two small synthetic tests (E37): a single-shot split is about as accurate as the ladder; the readout benefit under an identity shift is small and inconsistent. Both refuted. Update 2026-10-22 (E38-E41, docs/MINIMAL_CLAIMS_REPORT.md): at equal speeds the ladder splits every rung and a single-shot split does not (E38 confirmed); depth 5 holds with every check (E39 confirmed); the theory's invariance term did not make a generic MLP keep the fast block (E40 refuted). Update 2026-10-22 (E42): a variance term on each family's own block moved the fast block from absent to partial (0.27-0.52) but not to present (0 of 10); presence stays a stated precondition. Update 2026-10-23 (E43): enforcing the whitening constraint (which the execution had left out) and training longer made rung 1 clean on 9 of 10 and both rungs on 7 of 10 seeds for a generic MLP, but presence stayed below 0.95 (refuted as registered). Update 2026-10-23 (E44): the generic-MLP recipe holds to 4 and 5 blocks by the rung criteria (every rung clean on at least 7 of 10 seeds) but loses the slowest block (presence 0.56 and 0.33) and has dead output directions; mirror encoder keeps everything.
